        <lombok.version>1.18.48</lombok.version>
        <junit.version>5.13.4</junit.version>
        <maven-compiler-plugin.version>3.14.0</maven-compiler-plugin.version>
        <maven-surefire-plugin.version>3.5.3</maven-surefire-plugin.version>
    </properties>

    <dependencies>
        <!-- Compile-time only: generates getters/setters/constructors, not needed at runtime -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.projectlombok</groupId>
            <artifactId>lombok</artifactId>
            <version>${lombok.version}</version>
            <scope>provided</scope>
        </dependency>

        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
            <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>

            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>

                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-compiler-plugin</artifactId>

                    <!-- JDK 23+ no longer runs annotation processors found on the classpath
                         implicitly, so Lombok must be declared explicitly here. -->
                    <annotationProcessorPaths>
                        <path>
                            <groupId>org.projectlombok</groupId>
                            <artifactId>lombok</artifactId>
                            <version>${lombok.version}</version>
                        </path>
                    </annotationProcessorPaths>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>${maven-surefire-plugin.version}</version>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>
</project>
EOF

# Stop Lombok from looking for config files in parent directories

EOF
cat > src/main/java/com/example/app/model/User.java <<'EOF'
package com.example.app.model;

import lombok.AllArgsConstructor;
import lombok.Builder;
import lombok.Data;
import lombok.NoArgsConstructor;

/**
 * Mutable entity-style class. {@code @Data} generates getters, setters,
 * {@code equals}/{@code hashCode} and {@code toString}.
 */
@Data
@Builder
@NoArgsConstructor
@AllArgsConstructor
public class User {
    private Long id;
    private String name;
    private String email;
}
EOF
cat > src/main/java/com/example/app/model/Money.java <<'EOF'
package com.example.app.model;

import java.math.BigDecimal;

/**
 * Immutable value type. Prefer plain Java records for simple immutable data —
 * they need no Lombok at all.
 */
public record Money(BigDecimal amount, String currency) {
}
EOF
cat > src/test/java/com/example/app/model/UserTest.java <<'EOF'
package com.example.app.model;

import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

class UserTest {

    @Test
    void lombokGeneratesAccessorsConstructorsAndBuilder() {
        User viaBuilder = User.builder().id(1L).name("Ada").email("ada@example.com").build();
        User viaConstructor = new User(1L, "Ada", "ada@example.com");

        assertEquals(viaConstructor, viaBuilder);

        viaBuilder.setName("Grace");
        assertEquals("Grace", viaBuilder.getName());
    }
}
EOF
mvn -q -B verify 2>&1 | tail -30; echo EXIT=$?

content.text:
I set up a Maven project that uses **Lombok** to generate getters, setters and constructors. `mvn verify` passes, including a test that uses the generated builder, constructor, setter and getter.

**What's in it**
- **`pom.xml`**
  - Lombok 1.18.48 is a `provided` dependency, so it's only used at compile time and isn't packaged into the jar.
  - Lombok is also declared under the compiler plugin's `annotationProcessorPaths`. This is needed: from JDK 23 on, `javac` no longer runs annotation processors it finds on the classpath, so without it the annotations would do nothing.
  - The code compiles to Java 25. Tests use JUnit 6.1.3, and the compiler and surefire plugins are on their latest versions. A hook in this environment flagged my first versions as outdated, so I bumped them.
- **`lombok.config`**: stops Lombok reading config files from parent folders, and marks generated code with `@Generated` so coverage tools like JaCoCo skip it.
- **`User.java`**: a sample class using `@Data @Builder @NoArgsConstructor @AllArgsConstructor`. That gives you getters, setters, `equals`/`hashCode`/`toString`, both constructors and a builder.
- **`Money.java`**: a plain Java `record`. For simple immutable data, records remove the same boilerplate without Lombok, so the team may want them as the default and Lombok for mutable classes.
- **`UserTest.java`** and **`.gitignore`**.

**Things to know**
- The build prints a `sun.misc.Unsafe ... deprecated` warning from Lombok on recent JDKs. It's a known Lombok issue and the build is unaffected.
- IntelliJ includes Lombok support. In Eclipse or VS Code, each developer needs the Lombok plugin installed, or the IDE will show errors on generated methods.
- The group and package are placeholders (`com.example` / `app`); rename them to suit the team.

I haven't committed anything. I can commit it on a new branch if you want.

EOF
cat > lombok.config <<'EOF'
# Stop Lombok from looking for config files in parent directories
config.stopBubbling = true
# Mark generated code with @lombok.Generated so coverage tools (e.g. JaCoCo) ignore it
lombok.addLombokGeneratedAnnotation = true
EOF

target/

.classpath

EOF
cat > src/main/java/com/example/app/model/User.java <<'EOF'
package com.example.app.model;

import lombok.AllArgsConstructor;
import lombok.Builder;
import lombok.Data;
import lombok.NoArgsConstructor;

/**
 * Mutable entity-style class. {@code @Data} generates getters, setters,
 * {@code equals}/{@code hashCode} and {@code toString}.
 */
@Data
@Builder
@NoArgsConstructor
@AllArgsConstructor
public class User {
    private Long id;
    private String name;
    private String email;
}
EOF
cat > src/main/java/com/example/app/model/Money.java <<'EOF'
package com.example.app.model;

import java.math.BigDecimal;

/**
 * Immutable value type. Prefer plain Java records for simple immutable data —
 * they need no Lombok at all.
 */
public record Money(BigDecimal amount, String currency) {
}
EOF
cat > src/test/java/com/example/app/model/UserTest.java <<'EOF'
package com.example.app.model;

import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

class UserTest {

    @Test
    void lombokGeneratesAccessorsConstructorsAndBuilder() {
        User viaBuilder = User.builder().id(1L).name("Ada").email("ada@example.com").build();
        User viaConstructor = new User(1L, "Ada", "ada@example.com");

        assertEquals(viaConstructor, viaBuilder);

        viaBuilder.setName("Grace");
        assertEquals("Grace", viaBuilder.getName());
    }
}
EOF
